13.4 Curvature and Normal Vectors of a Curve
In this section we study how a curve turns or bends. To gain perspective, we look first at curves in the coordinate plane. Then we consider curves in space.
Curvature of a Plane Curve

As a particle moves along a smooth curve in the plane, T = dr>ds turns as the curve bends. Since T is a unit vector, its length remains constant and only its direction changes as the particle moves along the curve. The rate at which T turns per unit of length along the curve is called the curvature (Figure 13.17). The traditional symbol for the curvature function is the Greek letter k (“kappa”).
